summary.text: Paraskeva of Rome is remembered for preaching, steadfast confession and beheading. Her received life includes several imprisonments and miraculous deliverances before the final execution.

blocks.text: The OCA names her parents Agathon and Politia. She studies Scripture, distributes her inheritance after their deaths and preaches among pagans. The account places her first arrest under Antoninus Pius.
blocks.reason: Necessary concise biography and source-genre distinction. A substantial modern biography cannot be reproduced under an established licence; this is a source-bound summary, not its author’s wording.

blocks.text: The Des Moines parish account describes a Greek Christian household in Rome, secular and scriptural education, and study of philosophy. It says her parents died when she was twenty and that part of her inheritance supported a women’s community where she taught before travelling. These details are the parish’s received narrative, rather than independently documented contemporary records.
blocks.reason: Necessary concise biography and source-genre distinction. A substantial modern biography cannot be reproduced under an established licence; this is a source-bound summary, not its author’s wording.

blocks.text: The received life recounts a red-hot helmet and immersion in boiling oil and pitch. The emperor is burned while looking into the cauldron; after she heals him, he releases her. In another city, the governor Asclepius exposes her to a serpent, which dies after she makes the Cross.

blocks.text: GOARCH explains Paraskeve as preparation and connects her Friday birth-name with the Gospel’s day of Preparation. The following Gospel passage supplies that explicit biblical vocabulary; it is Scripture about Christ’s burial, not a biography of this later martyr.

blocks.text:
And now when the even was come, because it was the preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath,

Joseph of Arimathaea, an honourable counsellor, which also waited for the kingdom of God, came, and went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.

And Pilate marvelled if he were already dead: and calling unto him the centurion, he asked him whether he had been any while dead.

And when he knew it of the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.

And he bought fine linen, and took him down, and wrapped him in the linen, and laid him in a sepulchre which was hewn out of a rock, and rolled a stone unto the door of the sepulchre.

And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses beheld where he was laid.

blocks.text: Under a further governor, Tarasius, she is tortured and beheaded. The OCA gives140; the parish places the life approximately140–180. Those printed dates remain attributed and are not harmonized into an invented exact chronology.

blocks.text: The parish likewise distinguishes final beheading from earlier deliverances. It recounts the destruction of idols in Apollo’s temple before the execution.
